_meta.title: Viruddha Ahara — Incompatible Food Combinations in Ayurveda
_meta.description: Comprehensive listing of food incompatibilities (Viruddha Ahara) as described in classical Ayurvedic texts. These are deterministic safety rules that must be checked against every diet plan. Eighteen categories of incompatibility are recognized by Charaka.
_meta.primary_source: Charaka Samhita, Sutra Sthana, Chapter 26 (Atreyabhadrakapyiya Adhyaya)

severity_scale.critical: Can cause serious health issues. MUST be flagged and blocked.
severity_scale.high: Significant adverse effects. Should be flagged as a strong warning.
severity_scale.medium: Moderate adverse effects over time. Should be flagged as a warning.
severity_scale.low: Mild or context-dependent effects. Should be flagged as informational.

_meta.how_to_edit: Add new rules by appending to the appropriate array. Each rule needs: foods, condition, severity, effects, source. Run 'python -m ontology.verify' after changes.

categories_of_viruddha._description: Charaka describes 18 types of food incompatibility (Ashtadasha Viruddha). Source: Charaka Samhita Sutra 26.81-101.

types.description: Eating dry/sharp foods in dry regions, or oily/heavy foods in marshy regions
Eating cold/dry foods in winter, or hot/pungent foods in summer
Eating heavy food when Agni is weak, or light food when Agni is strong
Consuming honey and ghee in equal quantities by weight
Suddenly consuming foods one is not habituated to
Using foods/activities of similar qualities to one's aggravated dosha
Certain foods become toxic when processed a specific way (e.g., heated honey)
Combining foods of opposite potency (e.g., fish + milk: hot + cold)
Giving mild purgatives to hard bowel or strong purgatives to soft bowel
Eating Vata-aggravating food after exertion, or Kapha-aggravating food after sleep
Eating in wrong order — e.g., hot water after honey
Consuming cold things after having hot food, or vice versa
Consuming cold foods after ghee intake
Food cooked with bad fuel, undercooked, overcooked, or burnt
Mixing specific foods that produce toxicity together
Food that is unpleasant to taste or consumed unwillingly
Food that has lost its natural qualities through age or poor storage
Eating in public without proper cleanliness, or in a disturbed state of mind

effects: Produces a unique toxic effect (Gara Visha)
specific_food_incompatibilities.note: Honey and ghee are individually excellent but become toxic in equal proportions. Unequal proportions are acceptable.
specific_food_incompatibilities.source: Charaka Samhita, Sutra 26.84; Ashtanga Hridayam, Sutra 7.37

effects: Becomes toxic and indigestible when heated above 40°C
specific_food_incompatibilities.note: Honey should never be cooked, baked, or added to very hot liquids. Add to warm (not boiling) water or food only after it has cooled sufficiently.
specific_food_incompatibilities.source: Charaka Samhita, Sutra 26.84; Ashtanga Hridayam, Sutra 5.53

effects: Milk is cooling (Sheeta Virya), fish is heating (Ushna Virya)
specific_food_incompatibilities.note: This is one of the most cited Viruddha combinations. Applies to all types of fish with milk.
specific_food_incompatibilities.source: Charaka Samhita, Sutra 26.81; Sushruta Samhita, Sutra 20.16

specific_food_incompatibilities.note: Milk should not be combined with citrus fruits, tamarind, or other sour foods. This includes fruit smoothies with sour fruits and milk.

effects: Can aggravate Kapha and respiratory conditions
specific_food_incompatibilities.note: Despite the popularity of banana milkshakes, this combination is considered incompatible. If consumed, add cardamom or nutmeg to mitigate.
specific_food_incompatibilities.source: Ashtanga Hridayam, Sutra 7; Bhavaprakasha, Purva Khanda 6

specific_food_incompatibilities.note: Salty foods should not be taken with or immediately after milk.
Melons should generally be eaten alone, not combined with any other food.
Curd (yogurt) should not be heated directly. Buttermilk (takra) made from curd is acceptable as a processed form.

effects: Aggravates Kapha which is dominant at night
Can cause respiratory issues over time
specific_food_incompatibilities.note: If curd is desired at night, it should be mixed with honey, amla, ghee, or sugar to counteract. Buttermilk is a better alternative.

effects: Aggravates Pitta due to sour + hot season synergy
Can cause skin issues and acidity
specific_food_incompatibilities.note: In hot seasons, prefer buttermilk (takra) over curd. If consumed, add sugar and cooling spices.
Sugar (refined) with milk is acceptable; jaggery (gur) with milk is not ideal per classical texts.
Store ghee in glass, steel, or earthen vessels.

effects: Creates toxic effects similar to heating honey
specific_food_incompatibilities.note: Wait at least 30 minutes after consuming honey before having hot drinks.
Drink warm or room-temperature water after consuming ghee-rich meals.
Meals should not have equal proportions of fat/oil and watery elements.

effects: Both are heavy and can overload digestion

specific_food_incompatibilities.note: Common nightshades include eggplant, potato, tomato, bell pepper.
Do not combine fish + meat, or eggs + meat, or fish + eggs in one meal.
specific_food_incompatibilities.source: Charaka Samhita, Sutra 26; Sushruta Samhita, Sutra 20

seasonal_food_incompatibilities.reason: Vata is aggravated in cold seasons; cold and dry foods worsen imbalance.
seasonal_food_incompatibilities.prefer_instead: Warm, oily, nourishing foods with sweet, sour, and salty tastes.

seasonal_food_incompatibilities.reason: Pitta is already aggravated in summer; hot and pungent foods further inflame it.
seasonal_food_incompatibilities.prefer_instead: Cooling, sweet, liquid, and slightly oily foods. Coconut water, sweet fruits.

seasonal_food_incompatibilities.reason: Agni is weakest during monsoon (Vata aggravated). Heavy foods will not digest properly.
seasonal_food_incompatibilities.prefer_instead: Light, warm, freshly cooked foods with ginger and warming spices. Aged grains preferred.

seasonal_food_incompatibilities.reason: Kapha accumulated in winter melts and aggravates in spring. Heavy and sweet foods worsen this.
seasonal_food_incompatibilities.prefer_instead: Light, dry, warm, pungent, and bitter foods. Barley, honey, old grains.

dosha_specific_incompatibilities.reason: These foods share Vata's qualities and will further aggravate the imbalance.
These foods share Pitta's qualities and will further aggravate the imbalance.
These foods share Kapha's qualities and will further aggravate the imbalance.
